summary: The note defines a union territory as a type of administrative division in the Republic of India. Unlike states, which have elected governments of their own, union territories are ruled directly by the Union Government (central government), which is the source of the name. The note also states that union territories in India qualify as federal territories by definition.
one_line: Defines union territories, the administrative divisions of India ruled directly by the central Union Government rather than elected state governments.
key_facts: A union territory is a type of administrative division in the Republic of India.
Unlike states, union territories do not have their own elected governments.
Union territories are ruled directly by the Union Government (central government).
The name 'union territory' derives from being ruled directly by the Union Government.
Union territories in India qualify as federal territories, by definition.
